title: Flexible-duration license bands & upgrade-cadence playbook for Private/VPC pilots
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Define and validate a flexible licensing & support packaging playbook for Private/VPC and on-prem pilots that balances ARR predictability with enterprise procurement flexibility. Scope: license fee bands (term length + commit bands), support tiers (Standard / Priority / Concierge), upgrade cadence options (monthly security backports, quarterly minor, annual major), hotfix/upgrade credits, and the contract language needed to close pilot deals and answer standard security questionnaires for regulated customers.
primary_goals: Create 3 license-duration bands (12/24/36) with clear per-GPU and per-seat pricing anchors
Define 3 support tiers with SLA response/restore SLAs and an add-on for accelerated upgrades
Codify upgrade cadence options and an observable rollback/compatibility policy
Produce contract templates (SOW + addenda) and a pre-filled Security Questionnaire (V1) for sales
Run two pilot negotiations and collect quantitative feedback on willingness-to-pay and legal friction
acceptance_criteria: Pricing bands documented with unit economics and revenue recognition notes
Legal-approved contract addenda that cover upgrade windows, KMS/HSM obligations, and data residency clauses
Support tier matrix (SLAs, 24x7 vs business hours, escalation path) approved by SRE/Support leads
Security questionnaire v1 completed and placed in Sales enablement folder
At least two pilot customers signed on pilot terms or provided written objections that inform v2
decisions: Use term-based banding (12/24/36) instead of pure commit-size banding to reduce price negotiation points
Offer upgrade cadence as an explicit optional add-on to avoid forced major upgrades during pilot period
Include a fixed pool of upgrade/hotfix credits per term to reduce change-order friction
KMS/HSM obligations will be handled via an addendum rather than baked into base T&Cs to keep contract length manageable
tradeoffs: Longer term discounts improve ARR predictability but increase churn risk if upgrades are disruptive
Granular support tiers reduce over-servicing but add complexity to quoting and onboarding
Putting KMS/HSM into base contract simplifies procurement for some customers but creates legal risk surface for others
Automatic major upgrade mandates would lower technical debt but will block closed-airgap pilots; chosen to be optional
